recognize_zh: 周邊血液中多顆與紅血球差不多大的小型淋巴球，核質比極高、細胞質幾乎看不到，染色質呈粗塊狀、深淺交錯的「足球／龜殼狀」（soccer-ball）凝集，左上方並有一個 smudge cell，是典型 CLL 細胞。
features: Small lymphocytes approximately the size of a red cell
Very high N:C ratio with scant to barely visible cytoplasm
Round nuclei with coarse, block-like clumped chromatin (soccer-ball pattern)
Smudge cell in the upper field; red cells normocytic and normochromic
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows numerous small mature lymphocytes, roughly the size of a red cell, with very high nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio, round nuclei, and coarse, block-like clumped chromatin without nucleoli. A smudge cell is present. Prolymphocytes with prominent nucleoli are not seen in this field, and red cells are unremarkable. Findings are consistent with chronic lymphocytic leukemia; confirmation by flow cytometry is required.

ddx.vs: Normal lymphocytes look similar individually; CLL is recognized by absolute monotonous lymphocytosis with smudge cells and a clonal CD5+/CD23+ B-cell phenotype.
MCL cells typically have more irregular or notched nuclei and less clumped chromatin, and are cyclin D1-positive/CD23-negative.
Prolymphocytes are larger with moderately condensed chromatin and a single prominent central nucleolus, making up more than 15% in CLL/PL.
FL cells are small with deep nuclear clefts and are CD10-positive, CD5-negative.
